title: Interval DP
summary: Interval DP solves every contiguous range nums[i..j]. A range is built from shorter ranges inside it, so fill the table by length: all ranges of length 1, then 2, and so on up to the whole input.
idea: dp[i][j] = answer for the range i..j. Base: length 1. For each longer range, try the ends (or every split point k) and combine the shorter ranges. Answer: dp[0][n−1].

signals.see: The question is about a contiguous range that shrinks from either end: palindromes, removing from the ends, two-player games on a row.
signals.think: The state is a pair (i, j). Its answer comes from (i + 1, j) and (i, j − 1).

signals.see: You choose where to split or which item to handle last, and the cost depends on the whole range: cutting a stick, bursting balloons, merging piles.
signals.think: Try every split point k in i..j and combine dp[i][k] and dp[k][j] plus the cost of this step. That is O(n³).

signals.see: A greedy or left-to-right scan fails because a choice in the middle changes both sides.
signals.think: Ranges capture both sides at once. Fill by increasing length so the inner ranges are ready.

phrasings: Two players take turns removing a number from either end of a row. Can the first player win?
Find the longest subsequence that reads the same backwards.
Cut a stick at given marks, paying the current length for each cut. What is the least total cost?

picture.title: Left-to-right prefix versus ranges by length
picture.alt: On the left, a prefix DP moves left to right but cannot see choices made at the right end. On the right, dp[i][j] covers the range i to j and reads the two ranges one shorter, dp[i+1][j] and dp[i][j-1]; ranges are filled in order of length, so the whole row is solved last.
picture.caption: Fill short ranges first; each range reads ranges inside it.

visualiser.inputHelp: Up to 6 whole numbers from 0 to 20. The answer is the first player's best lead; below 0 means they lose.

oneLiner: for len in 1..n: for i: j = i+len-1; dp[i][j] = combine(dp[i+1][j], dp[i][j-1]) or split at k

exercise.prompt: Return how many substrings of s are palindromes. Substrings at different positions count separately, even when they spell the same thing. Use pal[i][j] for whether s[i..j] is a palindrome, filled by length. The starter only compares the two end letters.
hints: s[i..j] is a palindrome when its end letters match and the inside s[i + 1..j − 1] is a palindrome.
Ranges of length 1 and 2 have no inside to check: matching ends is enough.
Fill by length so the inside range is always decided first, and count every true cell.

complexity.why: There are about n²/2 ranges. When a range only reads its two shorter neighbours each cell is O(1); when it tries every split point k, each cell costs O(n).

mistakes: Filling row by row from i = 0, so dp[i + 1][j] is not ready yet. Fill by length, or loop i downwards.
Forgetting the length-1 base cases on the diagonal.
In two-player games, adding the opponent's best instead of subtracting it.
Off-by-one in the split loop: whether k is a cut position or the last item handled.

quiz.question: Why fill interval DP by increasing length?
choices: Each range reads ranges strictly inside it, which are shorter and so already filled
It is the only order that terminates
quiz.explain: Looping i from n − 1 down to 0 with j going up also works for the same reason.

quiz.question: In the ends game, why subtract dp[i + 1][j] after taking nums[i]?
choices: dp[i + 1][j] is the opponent's best lead on what is left, which counts against you
To avoid double counting the middle
It is a typo for addition
quiz.explain: Storing the lead of the player to move makes both players use the same table.

quiz.question: Cutting a stick at chosen marks: what does each range try?
choices: Every mark k inside it as the first cut, with dp[i][k] + dp[k][j] + the range's length
quiz.explain: Split-point interval DP tries every k, which gives O(n³).

interviewTip: Say 'the state is a range i..j and I fill it by length' up front. Then the only question is what each range tries: its two ends, or every split point.
